{{Quote|Rogues, listen up. Kasan has given us another Imperial military location. It's a large spaceport located at the end of this canyon. We're using Y-wings because of their greater firepower, but they move like a sleepy Hutt, so watch it.|Luke Skywalker, during the battle of Kile II|<ref name="RS I" />}}
The '''BTL-A4 Y-wing starfighter''' was the one-man version of the [[BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-S3]] [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] model.

==Characteristics==
The [[Koensayr Manufacturing/Legends|Koensayr]] [[BTL Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-A4]] Y-wing [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] was crewed by a single [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]].<ref name="EGW" /> The 16-[[Meter/Legends|meter]]-long attack starfighter had an [[ArMek/Legends|ArMek]] [[SW-4 ion cannon/Legends|SW-4 ion cannon]] turret which was preset to one of four arcs<ref name="DB" /> and was typically locked forward, although some pilots chose to lock it facing aft for extra cover.<ref name="SWSB">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> Easily modifiable,<ref name="RS I" /> the variant boasted much greater endurance (as much as three times greater) over its earlier predecessor, but was penalized with less powerful [[Deflector shield/Legends|deflector shields]] and loss of accuracy in the ion cannons.<ref name="RAS" /><ref name="SWSB" /> The loss of shield power provided a boost in [[Engine/Legends|engine]] power, but the combination proved insufficient and the Y-wing variant developed a poor reputation among its pilots,<ref name="EGW" /> and the starfighter was said to move like a "sleepy [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]."<ref name="RS I" /> Although slow for [[Starship/Legends|ship]]-to-ship combat,<ref name="RS II guide">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''</ref> it was still capable of [[Starfighter combat/Legends|engaging]] other craft,<ref name="DB" /> and the Y-wing was excellent when used for [[Planet/Legends|planetary]] [[Bomb/Legends|bombing]] runs.<ref name="RS II guide" />

The wedge-shaped cockpit and [[Guidenhauser/Legends|Guidenhauser]] [[Ejector seat/Legends|ejection system]] was placed on the front of the craft, with the central spar containing the [[Novaldex/Legends|Novaldex]] power generator extending behind it. [[Thiodyne/Legends|Thiodyne]] [[03-R cryogenic power cell/Legends|03-R cryogenic power cells]] and [[ionization reactor]] supplemented the Novaldex generator. Two 2 Koensayr [[R200 Ion Jet engine|R200 ion jet engines]], rated at 250 KTU<ref name="DB" /> and capable of 100 [[Megalight|MGLT]] were attached to either side of the spar. The engines had exhaust nacelles and support pylons,<ref name="RS I guide" /> and the [[Fabritech/Legends|Fabritech]] [[ANx-y long-range sensor array]] with [[PA-9r long-range phased tachyon detection array/Legends|PA-9r long range phased tachyon detection array]] and [[PG-7u short-range primary threat analysis grid/Legends|PG-7u short range primary threat analysis grid]]<ref name="DB" /> were placed in protective composite domes on the front of the nacelles.<ref name="RS I guide" /> The craft also had a Fabritech [[ANc 2.7 tracking computer/Legends|ANc 2.7 tracking computer]] with [[SI 5g7 "Quickscan" vector imaging system/Legends|SI 5g7 "Quickscan" vector imaging system]], and a [[Sublight Products Corporation|Subpro]] [[NH-7 flight control avionics package/Legends|NH-7 flight control avionics package]].<ref name="DB" /> Y-wings also carried supplies for one [[Standard week/Legends|week]] in 110 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] of weight.<ref name="RAS" /> The [[R300-H hyperdrive motivator/Legends|R300-H]] Class 1<ref name="DB" /> [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] was at the rear of the spar. The [[Chempat Shield Generator]] was also located on the spar.<ref name="RS I guide" /> Three [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] engines aided in maneuvering. The weapons were located in the cockpit: two [[Taim & Bak/Legends|Taim & Bak]] [[IX4 laser cannon/Legends|IX4]] or [[KX5 laser cannon/Legends|KX5 laser cannons]] along with two [[Arakyd Industries/Legends|Arakyd Industries]] [[Flex Tube proton torpedo launcher/Legends|Flex Tube proton torpedo launchers]] each with a magazine of four [[Proton torpedo/Legends|torpedoes]].<ref name="DB" /> The Y-wing could also carry 20 [[Proton bomb/Legends|proton bombs]].<ref name="RS I" /> The factory-fresh starfighters featured [[Armor/Legends|armor]]-plating around the central spar and the engines. [[Technician/Legends|Technicians]] eventually kept the panels removed to facilitate repairs.<ref name="CCS">''[[Star Wars: Complete Cross-Sections]]''</ref> [[Squadron/Legends|Squadron]] markings were placed on the cockpit and the forward tips of the engine nacelles.<ref name="DB" />

==History==
===Development===
[[File:KrailKaput-ANH.jpg|thumb|left|200px|[[Davish Krail/Legends|Davish Krail's]] Y-wing is destroyed at the Battle of Yavin.]]
The BTL-A4 Y-wing attack starfighter traces its lineage back to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[BTL-B Y-wing starfighter/Legends|BTL-B Y-wing starfighter]] used by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. After the war, the starfighter was put into service by [[Planetary Security Forces]]. As the resource-strapped [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] started to grow its resistance against the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]],<ref name="EGW" /> Y-wings started to be used more often, becoming the Rebel's primary starfighter.<ref name="RS I guide" /> The starfighters were brought into use by defecting Planetary Security Forces pilots, liberated from Imperial storehouses, or outright bought from [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] or unscrupulous [[Governor/Legends|governors]].<ref name="EGW" />

Y-wings were used since the earliest battles of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. A squadron joined in the [[Assault on Kamino|assault]] on the major Imperial [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] centers on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]]<ref name="TFU II novel">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (novelization)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' novelization]]</ref> in [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]].<ref name="TFU II comic">[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II (graphic novel)|''Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II'' graphic novel]]</ref> During the battle, [[Subject 1138|Starkiller]] rode on the outside of one piloted by the future [[Ace/Legends|ace]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] for a short time.<ref name="TFU II novel" />

===Battle of Yavin===
As the BTL-S3 became the primary Y-wing variant of the Rebel forces, the A4 was still kept in many units as a supplementary craft. Despite the existence of the BTL-S3, the BTL-A4 variant of the Y-wing was favored by [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Red]] and [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)/Legends|Gold Squadrons]], and served with distinction in many major battles.<ref name="X-W">[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|''Star Wars: X-Wing'']]</ref> They were the starfighter intended to destroy the first Death Star during the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. Flown by Gold Squadron, a trio of Y-wings were the first to launch a run into the trench to their target, an exhaust port leading to the main reactor, although the pilots were all shot down. Eventually, [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], in an [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]], succeeded in hitting the target.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> After the Battle of Yavin, the starfighters were assigned to less dangerous missions.<ref name="RS I guide" />

===Height of the Galactic Civil War===
{{Quote|Another hit like that and we've got it&hellip; Hull penetrated.|Wedge Antilles using a Y-wing to bomb the wreckage of the ''Motivator''|<ref name="RS II">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Starwarsrogueleader06.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Rogue Squadron flying BTL-A4s near The Maw]]
Members of [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] flew the BTL-A4 on strikes against Imperial targets, including the [[Kile II]] [[Spaceport/Legends|spaceport]] [[Assault on Kile II|assault]] and the [[Raid on Sullust|destruction]] of the capacitor on [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]].<ref name="RS I" /> After the Battle of Hoth and between [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Rogue Squadron used Y-wings on a [[Battle near the Maw|mission]] to [[Maw Cluster/Legends|The Maw]], and Antilles used one to bomb the Imperial ground forces and the hull of the crashed [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] [[Motivator (Imperial-class)|''Motivator'']] that was [[Battle of Kothlis|holding]] the [[CR90 corvette/Legends|CR90 corvette]] [[Razor (CR90 corvette)|''Razor'']].<ref name="RS II" /> Antilles also flew one during a [[Battle of Dubrillion (Galactic Civil War)|battle]] at [[Dubrillion/Legends|Dubrillion]] to destroy a [[Superlaser/Legends|superlaser]] threatening a Rebel fleet.<ref name="Rebel Strike">''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron III: Rebel Strike]]''</ref>

During that same time period, Rebel pilot [[Ace Azzameen/Legends|Ace Azzameen]] also flew the A4 Y-wing on missions, including a mission along with<ref name="XWA" /> the [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] [[Blue Squadron (Bothan)|Blue Squadron]]. The Bothans, sympathetic to the Rebellion and flying S3 Y-wings, participated in the capture of the Imperial [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] ''[[Suprosa]]'' during the [[Raid on the Suprosa|raid]] to capture a supercomputer containing the plans to the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]].<ref name="Shadows of the Empire (novel)">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref> More Y-wings were destroyed than any other Rebellion starfighter. The Y-wing was supplanted as the Rebellion, and later [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic's]], assault starfighter by the [[A/SF-01 B-wing starfighter/Legends|B-wing]]<ref name="DB" /> and [[BTL-S8 K-wing assault starfighter|K-wing]] starfighters.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:MCQ-ywing.png|thumb|left|200px|Concept art by Ralph McQuarrie]]
The Y-wing is based off concept art made by [[Ralph McQuarrie]]. The starfighters seen in the first ''Star Wars'' film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], were models produced by [[Industrial Light & Magic]] and filmed against bluescreens.

There is a discrepancy between two sources concerning the internal size of the main laser cannons. Y-Wing blueprints created during production of Star Wars: Episode IV show the internal laser cannons ending before the pilot's feet, whereas in ''[[Star Wars: Incredible Cross-Sections]]'' they continue throughout the entire cockpit.

''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]'' erroneously labels the A4 as the S3 version, as does ''[[Star Wars: Rogue Squadron II: Rogue Leader: The Official Nintendo Player's Guide]]''.
